title: ASRock Intel Arc B580 Challenger 12GB OC Graphics Card $419 + Delivery ($0 to Metro/ VIC, NSW, QLD C&C/ in-Store) @ Scorptec
body:
Deal: ASRock Intel Arc B580 Challenger 12GB OC Graphics Card $419 + Delivery ($0 to Metro/ VIC, NSW, QLD C&C/ in-Store) @ Scorptec

[supersabroso] Yep, this 2 year old card is only 3-15% better than a decade old Nvidia 1080 GTX 8GB. Tech advances quickly as modern card like the Radeon 9070 16GB ($979) is 60-250% faster than the 1080 GTX.

[Winny182] … I think they’re after more than just a case
[panda1010101] Easy then! If you wanna challenge yourself and DIY the PC, here's the part list:
CPU: 7500F Used for $130 via Aliexpress
Mobo: AM5 B650M (2 Ram Slots though) for $150
RAM: DDR5 1x8 or 2x8 6000mHz CL38 for $100ea
PSU: 700W Gold (you can go as low as 550w-600w as per reddit ) $76
SSD: M.2 NVME Gen4x4 SSD 500GB, with an endurance of TBW 300 for $110
CPU Cooler: Buy an AMD-branded Wraith Stealth cooler from facebook marketplace (negotiate $5-$10). Maybe seller would lend you their thermal paste?
Total price of $1045 with GPU + Case, 8GB DDR5 Ram.
[fordleg] @panda1010101: @panda1010101 thanks mate. Any pre builds that are compatible that require just the gpu to be put in? That you know of, im thinking sometime basic maybe around black friday hopefully im guessing the pcie 4.0 8x is important?
Cheers
[panda1010101] @fordleg: PCIe 4.0 and 5.0 is not important, and is not a bottleneck, for budget and mid-range GPUs like this one. Earlier this year there was a string of pre-build makers who posted deals on Ozbargain for their BYO-GPU deals, but they've whittled to nothing now. BYO GPU deals are very rare now, and you likely need to send a polite email to each prebuild maker to see if they can accommodate you.
[cryptowiz] Not sure how much you are willing to spend but, as a guide, you might want to look at what Scorptec (the seller of the video card) has put together as a gaming PC with this same video card. See here… https://www.scorptec.com.au/product/ready-to-run-pcs/gaming-…
They're charging $1,799 for the system but you (or a tech savvy friend) could put the same configuration together and maybe save some money, particularly if you have some of the components already and are just upgrading.

[panda1010101] With a mid-range CPU like the i5 12400F, expect 300fps 1080p High in CS2: link . Since CS2 is a competitive shooter, ideally you'd be playing low graphics 1080p, meaning a consistent 300fps with a 1% low of perhaps 200, a great result. There's not much benchmarks for those gacha games or roblox, but this GPU should do well.
[RSmith] @panda1010101: Thanks, how much RAM would I require. I have never built a PC before, but something I would like to do with my son.
[panda1010101] @RSmith: A hard but rewarding process. I suggest making a forum post in Computing: Discussion on Ozbargain, or r/ bapcaustralia, and asking for community support on how to DIY a PC. Also, refer to my advice for fordleg below.
How much RAM? For desktop/office work and light gaming, 8GB DDR5. For all gaming, light content creator workloads, 16gb DDR5.
To improve your knowledge about PCs, I recommend reviewing tech youtube channels like LinusTechTips or GamersNexus, and reading hardware reviews from TechPowerUp. This can help you tell what good PC components are, and what to avoid. A smart thing to do is make a list of good components, and buying them when they go on sale over the coming black friday period from retailers or e-commerce platforms.
[elusive] @RSmith: In the past I would've said 32GB minimum on a new build.
These days, I'd say 16GB in a budget build, and hope prices drop eventually.
8GB will "work" but likely be painful running even one or two applications (browser, Discord, etc.) in the background.
[mousie] It's a great value option and will do more titles than this.
[vid_ghost] Hardware unboxed has the B580 as being faster. around 20%
[HappyPuppies] In my opinion the 3060 is better for plug and play. The b580 drivers are janky. Also the 3060 is better on resale (if you ever want to upgrade).
[misunderstood98] Drivers were janky at release, although some brand new titles might have issues.
Personally I'd go this over a 3060 unless you're going LLM path. 3060ti is probably a better pick for 1080, but 1440 or 4k this still beats even the 3060ti.
[yak] If both are the same price, and you're buying this for gaming or general use, I'd go with the rtx3060 12GB. The nVidia card is slower than the B580, but the 3060 has wider support, a massive install base, and nVidia's upscaling/framegen.
If you enjoy tinkering with your card, or if you know that the Intel card can do whatever task you want of it (eg. you're buying it for game X that tests well on it, or multi-stream transcoding, or some other non-CUDA workload), or you want more fps for your $, then go Intel.
I'd probably go with the B580 for myself because I can do my own tinkering and tech support, but recommend the 3060 for anyone else. The 3060 is generally going to be a less painful user experience.
[safrane] Yes, AI vibe coding modders have added DLSS5 and multi-frame gen to older cards, so the 3060 is a solid buy. And long term support too as Intel will exit the discrete GPU market in favour of integrated graphics.
[misunderstood98] Thats speculation, Intel have unofficially only skipped celestial. Intel have not announced any cancellations.
Also that is bad advice, the 3060 non-ti doesn't even have double digit fps with dlss5. It's completely unplayable.
The b580 beats both the 3060 and the Ti version at 1440 and 4k, with the only caveat being LLM comparability with certain models that are cuda focused, but that is becoming rarer.

[Yuri Lowell] Maybe XBSX + 10% but depends on the game. B580 is comparable to a 6700 XT but XBSX between a 6700 and 6700 XT.
[yak] You can put this in a PCIe 3.0 slot and only see 1-3% dip in performance. PCIe 4.0 x8 is perfect for gaming with this card. PCIe 5.0 would gain you nothing.
[vanyellow] make sure resizable bar is on in eufi/bios
[yak] And if you don't have resizable bar in your stock BIOS, then you can often add it with a third party software tool. Typically a UEFI mod, I think. There's news articles and github repos about enabling this back in 2024. Even a decade old SuperMicro server board had Rebar added by modders.
[ozfool] @yak: Eh, the EUFI hack is pretty experimental and not guaranteed to work on all systems. I wouldn't advise people to rely on it.
Simpler to just not buy an Arc B580 unless you have reBar (and PCIE 4.0), i.e. most motherboards younger than 8 years old.
[HappyPuppies] Decent value, but I hesitate. Drivers are still janky, and experiences compatibility issues. It really wants rebar enabled, (some older motherboards dont support rebar) also alot of known quirks. The bigger issue is Intel’s GPU future is murky with credible reports the B580 could be end of life as Intel leans into Arc Pro/AI. Buy for now, but don’t buy expect longevity. Solid deal only if you’re OK with those caveats.

[vid_ghost] Intel have announced they are ending consumer cards and shifting all manufacturing to server data center GPU's
[misunderstood98] Intel haven't announced shit lol. Tech reviewers said the same thing after alchemist release, yet b580 followed.
Also since the b series, Intel have: opened new fabs, haven't locked down all the customers for their 18a nodes, started pushing 14a for next gen data centres. Plus Nvidia has announced they are stepping away from gaming… I wouldn't be surprised if (in the medium term) intel increase allocation of excess 18a for budget gaming.
While it wouldn't be a short term thing, I imagine it will be part of their wider push to remain competitive with AMD, who have really pushed the mobile gaming market and obviously secured the development of next gen consoles.
The only issue for AMD (and Bolt who are launching next year) is that they are fabless and rely entirely on TSMC. Intel don't have this problem. Given they rehired Demers to extend the R&D of their current tiles, if they can find an answer to the ram crisis (which isn't lpddr5x sadly - as that eats wafer capacity), Intel are in a unique position to 'soak up' the budget gaming market with their upcoming tiles. xe3p already showing amazing results for budget gaming.
If intel do secure apple and Nvidia contracts though, we might be waiting a longer time - but even still, I am more bullish than the avg market sentiment with regard to future gaming products, despite the negative indicators from Nvidia and the 'ai bubble'.
Anyways this is all a while away, as yields are still low. 2027 will definitely be the worst year for the average pc builder.

[misunderstood98] On newer kernels it's relatively smooth now, even more so since SteamOS started supporting Intel, the last few months intel dgpus have been aging like wine.
Funnily enough, steamOS was a breath of fresh air for intel devs after the Crimson Desert drama that plagued their reputation.
In saying that, I do believe there was some underhanded behaviour from AMD that caused those issues though (given the dismay shown by the intel driver team noting they reached out to developers several times). That behaviour unheard of in the past from teams Red, Green or Blue - but it definitely wasn't something people were expecting in 2026.
